title: Which of these converge uniformly?

prereqs.why: Uniform convergence is convergence of the suprema, and every line is decided by computing one.
The supremum norm is the metric in which uniform convergence is ordinary convergence.

statement:
Each line gives a sequence of functions $(f_n)$ and a set. In every case
$(f_n)$ converges **pointwise** on that set.

Select every line on which the convergence is also **uniform**, that is, on
which

$$\sup_{x} \bigl|f_n(x) - f(x)\bigr| \longrightarrow 0$$

where $f$ is the pointwise limit.
hints: Find the pointwise limit first — it is $0$ on four of the six lines — and then maximise $|f_n - f|$ over the stated set.
For $x^n$ the behaviour on $[0,\tfrac12]$ and on $[0,1]$ is completely different, and the difference is entirely at the right-hand endpoint.
A bump of fixed height that moves off to the right has supremum equal to its height at every $n$, however far away it has gone.
